decisions.replacement_text: BIRC3::MALT1, historically called API2::MALT1, is the t(11;18)-associated fusion in a subset of gastric MALT lymphomas.

evidence.location: Results: t(11;18) detection; Figure 2; PDF pages 3-4
evidence.scope: Fusion transcripts measured by RT-PCR/sequencing in patient gastric MALT specimens.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: The t(11;18) fusion joins BIRC3 BIR domains to MALT1 signaling/paracaspase regions and activates NF-kappaB signaling. It occurs in extranodal marginal zone lymphoma, especially gastric and pulmonary MALT lymphoma.

decisions.label: BIRC3::MALT1
decisions.replacement_text: In the 111-patient gastric MALT cohort, t(11;18)/API2::MALT1 was strongly associated with failure of lymphoma regression after H. pylori eradication.

evidence.location: Results: t(11;18) detection and response; Figure 3; Table 2; PDF pages 3-5
evidence.scope: Actual antibiotic-treatment outcomes, including transiently regressing fusion-positive cases.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: In gastric MALT lymphoma, t(11;18)/BIRC3::MALT1 is associated with reduced likelihood of lymphoma regression after Helicobacter pylori eradication.

decisions.label: IGH / MYC

evidence.scope: All three IG partners directly detected in WGS cohort; indexed Results passage inspected.

decisions.original_text: The rearrangement places MYC under immunoglobulin regulatory control, increasing MYC expression and proliferative transcription. It is characteristic of Burkitt lymphoma but also occurs in other B-cell neoplasms.

decisions.label: IGH / BCL6
decisions.replacement_text: IGH/BCL6 juxtaposition has been directly demonstrated in a subset of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma specimens by combined immunophenotyping and fluorescence in situ hybridization.

decisions.original_text: The rearrangement substitutes immunoglobulin regulatory elements for normal BCL6 control, sustaining BCL6-dependent transcriptional repression. BCL6 rearrangements occur in several B-cell lymphomas and are not specific to one histologic type.

evidence.location: Results: EWS-FLI1 binding sites; Figure 1

decisions.original_text: The fusion replaces the SS18 carboxy terminus with SSX sequences and redirects BAF chromatin-remodeling complexes, activating an oncogenic transcriptional program. It is a defining molecular alteration of synovial sarcoma.

decisions.original_text: Afamitresgene autoleucel is US-approved for adults with unresectable or metastatic synovial sarcoma after chemotherapy who have one of the specified HLA-A*02 alleles and whose tumors express MAGE-A4. decisions.original_text: The fusion combines paired-box DNA binding with the FOXO1 transactivation region, generating a potent abnormal transcription factor that drives fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma.

decisions.label: COL1A1::PDGFB

evidence.location: Results; Tables 1–3; Figure 1
evidence.scope: COL1A1-PDGFB-associated advanced DFSP including fibrosarcomatous tumors; responses to imatinib.

decisions.replacement_text: COL1A1::PDGFB is a recurrent fusion in dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, including fibrosarcomatous tumors.
decisions.original_text: The fusion places PDGFB under COL1A1 regulatory control, leading to excess PDGF-B ligand and autocrine PDGFRB activation. It is characteristic of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, including fibrosarcomatous examples.

decisions.label: COL1A1::PDGFB

decisions.original_text: Imatinib has demonstrated clinical activity in advanced or unresectable fusion-associated dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans by inhibiting PDGFRB signaling. The drug targets the activated receptor, not the PDGFB ligand.

decisions.label: NAB2::STAT6

evidence.location: Results; Figures 1, 3 and 4; Table 1

decisions.replacement_text: NAB2::STAT6 joins NAB2 EGR-binding sequences to the STAT6 activation region. In experimental assays the fusion activates EGR1-responsive transcription; it is recurrent in solitary fibrous tumor and shows nuclear localization.
decisions.original_text: The intrachromosomal fusion combines NAB2 EGR-binding sequences with STAT6 activation sequences, converting a transcriptional repressor complex into an activator. It is the defining molecular alteration of solitary fibrous tumor and underlies characteristic nuclear STAT6 staining.

decisions.replacement_text: ASPSCR1::TFE3 acts as an oncogenic transcriptional regulator in alveolar soft part sarcoma: fusion-degradation experiments alter cell-cycle, mitochondrial and angiogenic expression programs. The fusion also occurs in TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma.
decisions.original_text: The fusion joins ASPSCR1 sequences to the TFE3 transcription-factor region, generating an abnormal transcriptional activator. It is characteristic of alveolar soft part sarcoma and also occurs in TFE3-rearranged renal cell carcinoma.

decisions.original_text: Atezolizumab is US-approved for unresectable or metastatic alveolar soft part sarcoma from age 2 years. This histology-specific indication does not extend to TFE3-rearranged renal carcinoma.

EWSR1::ATF1 occurs in clear cell sarcoma and several distinct epithelial or mesenchymal tumors, including angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma and salivary hyalinizing clear cell carcinoma.

decisions.original_text: The fusion combines a FET-family activation region with a CREB-family DNA-binding region, producing abnormal transcriptional activation. EWSR1::CREB1 is a recognized fusion in angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma.

decisions.original_text: The fusion joins the EWSR1 activation region to NFATC2 DNA-binding sequences. It identifies a molecularly distinct EWSR1::non-ETS sarcoma, often arising in long bones, rather than conventional Ewing sarcoma.

decisions.label: EWSR1::PATZ1

evidence.location: Results; Table 1; molecular results

decisions.original_text: The fusion combines EWSR1 activation sequences with PATZ1 DNA-binding/regulatory regions. Reported sarcomas often show mixed neural, myogenic or epithelial marker expression and are distinct from conventional Ewing sarcoma.

decisions.original_text: The fusion joins HEY1 DNA-binding/repressor-associated sequences to NCOA2 transcriptional activation regions, creating a disease-associated transcriptional regulator. It is a recurrent defining alteration in mesenchymal chondrosarcoma.

decisions.label: JAZF1::SUZ12

evidence.location: Results; Figures 1–3

decisions.original_text: The fusion alters SUZ12-associated Polycomb complex assembly, chromatin occupancy and repression. It is recurrent in low-grade endometrial stromal tumors, including both stromal nodules and sarcomas; invasion distinguishes these categories.

decisions.label: YWHAE::NUTM2A

decisions.original_text: The fusion joins YWHAE to a NUTM2-family partner, producing an abnormal transcription-associated protein. It defines a major high-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma group, often with a high-grade round-cell component and strong cyclin D1/BCOR expression.

decisions.label: PML::RARA
decisions.replacement_text: PML::RARA blocked IL-3-stimulated myeloid differentiation in experimental marrow systems; ATRA restored differentiation. Coexpression with IL-3 produced rapidly fatal AML-like disease in transplanted mice.

evidence.location: Results; Figure 2 differentiation and ATRA rescue; Figures 3-4 murine leukemia
evidence.scope: Root inspected direct functional and transplant results; does not equate model assays with clinical response rate.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The t(15;17) fusion alters retinoic-acid-dependent transcription, recruits repressive chromatin machinery and disrupts PML nuclear bodies, producing a block in promyelocyte differentiation. It is the defining driver of conventional acute promyelocytic leukemia.

decisions.label: RUNX1::RUNX1T1
decisions.replacement_text: RUNX1::RUNX1T1 (AML1-ETO) promotes serial replating of murine hematopoietic progenitors. DNA-binding disruption or deletion of its NHR2 oligomerization region abolished this transforming activity in the tested model.

evidence.location: Results; Figures 2,4,5
evidence.scope: Root inspected full body: serial replating, DNA-binding mutant and NHR2 deletion functional comparisons. Model-bounded mechanism.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The t(8;21) fusion combines RUNX1 DNA binding with RUNX1T1 transcriptional repression, altering hematopoietic differentiation. It defines a core-binding factor AML subtype.

decisions.label: CBFB::MYH11
decisions.replacement_text: CBFB::MYH11 formed cytoplasmic aggregates that recruited RUNX1 in hematopoietic-cell models. Immunofluorescence of primary fusion-positive AML samples also supported predominantly cytoplasmic localization.

evidence.location: Results: RUNX1 colocalizes with cytoplasmic CBFB::MYH11; Figures 4 and 5A-B; Supplemental Figures 2-3
evidence.scope: Model domain comparisons plus actual primary AML imaging; no claim that RUNX1 function is simply extinguished.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The inv(16)/t(16;16) fusion alters CBFB interaction with RUNX1 and core-binding factor transcription, impairing myeloid differentiation. It is associated with AML showing myelomonocytic differentiation and abnormal eosinophils.

decisions.label: DEK::NUP214
decisions.replacement_text: DEK::NUP214 bound regulatory regions of FOXC1 and HOXA/HOXB genes in cellular models. XPO1 inhibition reduced fusion-associated binding and expression of these leukemia-associated transcriptional targets, including in primary t(6;9) AML samples.

evidence.location: Results and Discussion: XPO1-dependent transcription factor; Figure 2B-F; PDF pages 4-6
evidence.scope: Direct CUT&RUN and perturbation evidence; XPO1 inhibitor sensitivity is experimental and not a fusion-specific approved treatment.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The t(6;9) fusion links DEK to the carboxy-terminal region of NUP214, producing an abnormal nuclear protein that alters transcriptional and proliferative programs. It defines a recurrent AML subtype and often co-occurs with FLT3-ITD.

decisions.label: RBM15::MRTFA

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The t(1;22) fusion joins an RNA-associated regulator to a serum-response-factor coactivator and dysregulates hematopoietic transcription. It is characteristic of a subset of infant non-Down-syndrome acute megakaryoblastic leukemia.

decisions.label: CBFA2T3::GLIS2
decisions.replacement_text: CBFA2T3::GLIS2 was identified in pediatric non-Down-syndrome acute megakaryoblastic leukemia by molecular screening in an international cohort.

evidence.location: Results: molecular subgroups; Figure 1 and Figure 2D-F
evidence.scope: Direct ordered-fusion detection in pediatric AMKL; does not establish a universal lineage phenotype.

It is associated with megakaryoblastic disease and the RAM immunophenotype, including strong CD56 and weak or absent CD45/CD38.

decisions.label: NPM1::MLF1
decisions.replacement_text: Patient-derived NPM1::MLF1 fusion constructs showed aberrant cytoplasmic localization and promoted myeloid leukemogenesis in experimental models, with HOX activation linked to XPO1.

evidence.location: Results: NPM1 fusion proteins localize to the cytoplasm and promote myeloid leukemogenesis; Figures 1-2; HOX reporter/ChIP and XPO1 perturbation Results
evidence.scope: Direct fusion constructs, localization, leukemic model and HOX experiments; not a clinical inhibitor indication.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The t(3;5) fusion joins amino-terminal NPM1 sequences to MLF1 and alters intracellular regulation in hematopoietic cells. It is a rare recurrent AML fusion, distinct from the common NPM1 exon 12 mutation.

decisions.label: RUNX1::MECOM

evidence.scope: Direct diagnosis and sequenced fusion; does not generalize a single case to all myeloid contexts.

decisions.original_text: The t(3;21) fusion combines RUNX1 DNA-binding sequences with MECOM/EVI1 transcriptional-regulatory sequences, disrupting hematopoietic differentiation. It occurs in myeloid neoplasia, including therapy-related disease and CML blast phase.

decisions.label: KMT2A::MLLT3
decisions.replacement_text: KMT2A::MLLT3 is a recurrent KMT2A fusion in acute leukemia, documented by genomic breakpoint analysis in a large patient cohort.

evidence.location: Results; Table 1; Figure 2; disease distributions at lines 810-825
evidence.scope: Patient-level detection and recurrent partner distribution; no blanket proof of menin/HOXA/MEIS1 mechanism.

decisions.original_text: The t(16;21)(p11;q22) fusion combines the FUS transcriptional activation region with ERG DNA-binding sequences, creating an aberrant ETS transcription factor. It defines a rare AML subtype distinct from RUNX1::CBFA2T3 AML.

decisions.label: FUS::ERG
decisions.replacement_text: Pediatric FUS::ERG AML has shown poor outcomes and frequent relapse in the international I-BFM cohort.

evidence.location: Results, outcome analyses; Table 1/Figure 1 and multivariable model, PDF pages 3-4
evidence.scope: High relapse and poor pediatric outcomes.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: Pediatric FUS::ERG AML has shown poor outcomes and frequent relapse in the international I-BFM cohort.

decisions.label: FUS::ERG
decisions.replacement_text: FUS::ERG also occurs in Ewing sarcoma: an RNA-based fusion panel confirmed the exact fusion in a reported renal Ewing sarcoma.

evidence.location: Case report diagnostic workup; Figures 2-3
evidence.scope: Actual patient FUS FISH followed by 507-gene RNA fusion-panel confirmation; primary-case diagnostic section inspected in indexed fulltext.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: FUS::ERG also occurs rarely in Ewing sarcoma. The adverse AML outcome association below applies to pediatric leukemia, not to all tumors with this pair.

decisions.label: KAT6A::CREBBP
decisions.replacement_text: The fusion joins KAT6A to an acetyltransferase-associated coactivator. Domain-preserving fusion constructs induced AML in mice and altered chromatin-associated transcription in experimental models.

evidence.location: Results: Development of K/C and K/P murine leukemia models; Figures 1,3,6
evidence.scope: Fusion-construct oncogenicity and chromatin-associated transcription; not validation of all clinical phenotypic claims.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: The fusion joins two acetyltransferase-associated transcriptional regulators, redirecting chromatin acetylation and leukemogenic gene expression. KAT6A fusions are associated with monocytic differentiation, erythrophagocytosis and sometimes disseminated intravascular coagulation.

decisions.label: KAT6A::CREBBP
decisions.replacement_text: Adult AML with KAT6A::CREBBP is assigned adverse ELN 2022 genetic risk.

evidence.location: Table 6, 2022 ELN risk classification by genetics at initial diagnosis
evidence.scope: Favorable CBF; intermediate t(9;11); adverse DEK::NUP214, other KMT2A, MECOM and KAT6A::CREBBP categories.

decisions.rationale: Removed neonatal spontaneous-remission subclaim pending direct primary review.
decisions.original_text: Adult AML with KAT6A::CREBBP is assigned adverse ELN 2022 genetic risk. Congenital cases can have a distinct course, including reported spontaneous remissions.

decisions.label: NPM1::ALK
decisions.replacement_text: In a conditional NPM1::ALK mouse model, fusion expression induced lymphoma with activation of MYC- and NOTCH1-associated programs. Dnmt1 deletion prevented lymphoma development despite persistent proximal ALK signaling.

evidence.location: Results: Induction of ALK-dependent tumorigenic pathways; Figure 1 RNA-seq/qPCR; Figure 3 Dnmt1 deletion and pSTAT3
evidence.scope: Primary mouse-model gene expression and genetic-dependency assays inspected by root and body accessed by delegated reviewer; no universal human clinical dependency inferred.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion uses NPM1-mediated oligomerization to activate the ALK kinase and downstream survival pathways. It is the principal fusion in ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma.

decisions.label: NPM1::ALK
decisions.replacement_text: Crizotinib has a US indication for children aged at least 1 year and young adults with relapsed or refractory systemic ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma.

evidence.location: Prescribing information section 1.2
evidence.scope: Actual ALK-positive ALCL indication; not a fusion-specific label.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: Crizotinib has a US indication for relapsed or refractory systemic ALK-positive anaplastic large cell lymphoma in children aged at least 1 year and young adults. Its efficacy and safety for that indication were not established in older adults in the cited label.

decisions.label: BCR::ABL1
decisions.replacement_text: Expression of p210 BCR::ABL1 in transplanted murine bone marrow induced a CML-like myeloproliferative syndrome, demonstrating its leukemogenic activity in vivo. Other hematologic tumor phenotypes also occurred in the model.

evidence.location: Results, page 825; Table 1; Figures 2-3
evidence.scope: Root inspected primary PDF CML-like disease, proviral analyses and tumor phenotypes; does not independently prove all human isoform frequencies.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The Philadelphia-chromosome rearrangement joins the BCR oligomerization region to the ABL1 kinase, generating constitutive tyrosine-kinase signaling. It defines CML and a major B-ALL subtype; p210 and p190 are common transcript products.

decisions.label: BCR::ABL1
decisions.replacement_text: ABL tyrosine-kinase inhibitors are incorporated into treatment of BCR::ABL1-positive ALL.

evidence.location: Treatment of newly diagnosed Ph-positive ALL
evidence.scope: ALL treatment recommendation; removed broad resistance-sequencing assertions.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: ABL1-directed tyrosine-kinase inhibitors are established treatment components in CML and Philadelphia-positive ALL. Fusion transcript quantification also provides a molecular response marker.

decisions.label: ETV6::RUNX1
decisions.replacement_text: ETV6::RUNX1 defines a recurrent pediatric B-ALL subgroup documented by genomic profiling in a large patient cohort.

evidence.location: Results: Correlation between genetic alteration and disease subgroup; supplemental Figure 6
evidence.scope: Direct genomic subgroup assignment: ETV6RUNX1 n236; TCF3PBX1 n95; no untested biochemical mechanism.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The cryptic t(12;21) fusion combines ETV6 repressive activity with RUNX1 DNA-binding regions and perturbs B-cell differentiation. It is a common initiating lesion in childhood B-ALL and can arise prenatally.

decisions.label: TCF3::PBX1
decisions.replacement_text: TCF3::PBX1 defines a recurrent pediatric B-ALL subgroup documented by genomic profiling in a large patient cohort.

evidence.location: Results: Correlation between genetic alteration and disease subgroup; supplemental Figure 6
evidence.scope: Direct genomic subgroup assignment: ETV6RUNX1 n236; TCF3PBX1 n95; no untested biochemical mechanism.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The t(1;19) fusion joins the TCF3 activation region to the PBX1 homeodomain, creating an abnormal transcription factor. It defines a recurrent B-ALL subtype, often with a pre-B phenotype.

decisions.label: ETV6::RUNX1
decisions.replacement_text: In St. Jude Total XV, ETV6::RUNX1-positive B-ALL had better event-free and overall survival than fusion-negative disease. This difference was not significant in the earlier Total XIIIA/B cohorts, supporting a treatment-specific interpretation.

evidence.location: Results: Response and outcome; Figure 1; prognostic features/Table 3, lines 303-335
evidence.scope: Actual comparative cohort survival across successive protocols; no claim of an invariant independent genotype effect.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: ETV6::RUNX1-positive childhood B-ALL generally has favorable outcomes with contemporary chemotherapy, although late relapse occurs.

decisions.label: TCF3::PBX1
decisions.replacement_text: In the St. Jude cohort, TCF3::PBX1-positive B-ALL had event-free survival comparable to other B-cell-precursor ALL but a higher incidence of CNS relapse. The CNS association persisted in the study multivariable analyses.

evidence.location: Results: clinical outcomes and CNS relapse; Figure 1; multivariable analysis paragraph
evidence.scope: Direct 41-fusion-positive-patient comparison; protocol-specific relapse pattern, not universal poor survival.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: Outcomes have improved with intensive modern ALL therapy; historical adverse-risk estimates should not be applied to current regimens. Adult ELN 2024 describes favorable outcomes with intensive therapy.

decisions.label: EP300::ZNF384
decisions.replacement_text: EP300::ZNF384 was documented in B-ALL with weak CD10 and aberrant myeloid-marker expression in a targeted clinical cohort. The junction was confirmed by RT-PCR and sequencing.

evidence.location: Results; Table 1 partner and immunophenotype columns; Figure 1A-B and 1D
evidence.scope: Ordered pair and measured phenotype; selected CD10-low cohort. Excludes unsupported generalized MPAL frequency or lineage-conversion mechanism.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion joins a transcriptional-regulatory partner to ZNF384 and alters hematopoietic lineage programs. ZNF384-rearranged leukemia often shows weak CD10 with aberrant CD13/CD33 expression and can have B-lineage/myeloid phenotypic overlap.

decisions.label: TCF3::ZNF384
decisions.replacement_text: TCF3::ZNF384 was documented in B-ALL with weak CD10 and aberrant myeloid-marker expression in a targeted clinical cohort. The reported TCF3 partner was identified by FISH.

evidence.location: Results; Table 1 partner and immunophenotype columns; Figure 1A-B and 1D
evidence.scope: Ordered pair and measured phenotype; selected CD10-low cohort. Excludes unsupported generalized MPAL frequency or lineage-conversion mechanism.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion joins a transcriptional-regulatory partner to ZNF384 and alters hematopoietic lineage programs. ZNF384-rearranged leukemia often shows weak CD10 with aberrant CD13/CD33 expression and can have B-lineage/myeloid phenotypic overlap.

decisions.label: TAF15::ZNF384
decisions.replacement_text: TAF15::ZNF384 was documented in B-ALL with weak CD10 and aberrant myeloid-marker expression in a targeted clinical cohort. The junction was confirmed by RT-PCR and sequencing.

evidence.location: Results; Table 1 partner and immunophenotype columns; Figure 1A-B and 1D
evidence.scope: Ordered pair and measured phenotype; selected CD10-low cohort. Excludes unsupported generalized MPAL frequency or lineage-conversion mechanism.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion joins a transcriptional-regulatory partner to ZNF384 and alters hematopoietic lineage programs. ZNF384-rearranged leukemia often shows weak CD10 with aberrant CD13/CD33 expression and can have B-lineage/myeloid phenotypic overlap.

decisions.label: PAX5::ETV6
decisions.replacement_text: PAX5::ETV6 is a recurrent in-frame fusion in the PAX5-altered B-ALL subgroup, identified in 19 cases in a large genomic study.

evidence.location: Results: PAX5 alterations; Figure 2A; Supplementary Table 6
evidence.scope: Exact recurrent partner and expressed in-frame fusion in patient B-ALL, not merely PAX5 gene-level alterations.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion joins PAX5 DNA-binding sequences to ETV6 regulatory regions, impairing normal PAX5-dependent B-cell differentiation. It is a recurrent lesion within PAX5-altered B-ALL.

decisions.label: SET::NUP214
decisions.replacement_text: SET::NUP214 is a recurrent T-ALL fusion. In LOUCY cells, fusion knockdown reduced HOXA expression and proliferation and increased differentiation markers; ChIP detected association with HOXA9 and HOXA10 promoters.

evidence.location: Results: SET-NUP214 activates HOXA expression; direct HOXA activation; Figures 5A-G and 6A
evidence.scope: Knockdown and promoter-binding results; DOT1L recruitment was proposed rather than causally established.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion produces a SET-containing NUP214 protein that perturbs nuclear-export-associated transcription and is linked to HOXA activation. It is found in immature T-lineage leukemia and some AML cases.

decisions.label: FIP1L1::PDGFRA
decisions.replacement_text: FIP1L1::PDGFRA was documented in 78 patients in a registry study of myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with tyrosine-kinase fusions, providing direct clinical evidence for this disease association.

evidence.location: Results: Patient characteristics; Table 1
evidence.scope: All PDGFRA cases in this cohort had exact FIP1L1 partner; no independent kinase-domain functional proof asserted.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: A cryptic 4q12 deletion joins FIP1L1 to PDGFRA and disrupts PDGFRA juxtamembrane autoinhibition, creating a constitutively active kinase. It commonly presents as a myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia.

decisions.label: ETV6::PDGFRB
decisions.replacement_text: ETV6::PDGFRB was identified in 18 patients in a 26-patient cohort of PDGFRB-rearranged myeloid neoplasms, predominantly chronic myeloproliferative or myelomonocytic disease with eosinophilia.

evidence.location: Results, first paragraph and Table 1
evidence.scope: Exact fusion partner frequencies and cohort morphologic diagnoses; no independent functional mechanism inferred.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion couples ETV6 oligomerization to the PDGFRB kinase, driving ligand-independent signaling. It occurs in myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms that often show eosinophilia or a chronic myelomonocytic presentation.

decisions.label: ZMYM2::FGFR1
decisions.replacement_text: ZMYM2::FGFR1 was a recurrent fusion identified among FGFR1-rearranged myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms in a registry cohort.

evidence.location: Results: patients with FGFR1 fusion genes; Table 1
evidence.scope: Among six partner-characterized cases, ZMYM2 occurred in three and BCR in two; direct pair-to-disease observation.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion retains the FGFR1 kinase and replaces receptor control with a partner-derived self-association region, producing constitutive signaling. FGFR1-rearranged neoplasms can involve myeloid disease and lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia, with progression to blast phase.

decisions.label: BCR::FGFR1
decisions.replacement_text: BCR::FGFR1 was a recurrent fusion identified among FGFR1-rearranged myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms in a registry cohort.

evidence.location: Results: patients with FGFR1 fusion genes; Table 1
evidence.scope: Among six partner-characterized cases, ZMYM2 occurred in three and BCR in two; direct pair-to-disease observation.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion retains the FGFR1 kinase and replaces receptor control with a partner-derived self-association region, producing constitutive signaling. FGFR1-rearranged neoplasms can involve myeloid disease and lymphoblastic lymphoma/leukemia, with progression to blast phase.

decisions.label: PCM1::JAK2
decisions.replacement_text: PCM1::JAK2 was documented in a clinical series of JAK2-fusion myeloid neoplasms presenting in chronic or blast phase, often with marrow fibrosis and abnormal erythropoiesis.

evidence.location: Results 3.1, Table 1 and Figure 1; PDF pages 3-5
evidence.scope: Actual partner-confirmed patient series and morphologic features; no experimental constitutive-kinase proof inferred.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion retains the JAK2 tyrosine-kinase region and removes normal amino-terminal control, producing constitutive JAK-STAT signaling. PCM1::JAK2 is associated with myeloid/lymphoid neoplasia.

decisions.label: FIP1L1::PDGFRA
decisions.replacement_text: Imatinib can induce durable hematologic, cytogenetic and molecular remissions in FIP1L1::PDGFRA-associated myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms.

evidence.location: Table 1, PDGFRA/PDGFRB rows; Treatment, PDF pages 3-5
evidence.scope: Guideline synthesis of fusion-class clinical response, not independently reviewed trial.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: FIP1L1::PDGFRA is highly imatinib-sensitive, with durable hematologic and molecular responses reported in clinical studies.

decisions.label: ETV6::PDGFRB
decisions.replacement_text: A PDGFRB-rearranged myeloid-neoplasm cohort, including 18 ETV6::PDGFRB cases, showed frequent and durable responses to imatinib; outcomes were reported for the pooled fusion cohort.

evidence.location: Results: Table 1; response paragraphs and dose-reduction follow-up
evidence.scope: Observed pooled imatinib responses; avoids converting class outcomes into partner-specific rates.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: Imatinib has produced durable long-term remissions in PDGFRB-fusion-positive myeloid neoplasms, including ETV6::PDGFRB disease.

decisions.label: ZMYM2::FGFR1
decisions.replacement_text: Pemigatinib has a US indication for adults with relapsed or refractory myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with FGFR1 rearrangement.

evidence.location: Prescribing information section 1.2, PDF page 2
evidence.scope: Correct adult relapsed/refractory FGFR1-rearranged MLN indication.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: Pemigatinib is US-approved for adults with relapsed or refractory myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms harboring an FGFR1 rearrangement. ZMYM2 and BCR were frequent partners in FIGHT-203.

decisions.label: BCR::FGFR1
decisions.replacement_text: Pemigatinib has a US indication for adults with relapsed or refractory myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with FGFR1 rearrangement.

evidence.location: Prescribing information section 1.2, PDF page 2
evidence.scope: Correct adult relapsed/refractory FGFR1-rearranged MLN indication.

decisions.rationale: Retained only the statement supported at the recorded source location.
decisions.original_text: Pemigatinib is US-approved for adults with relapsed or refractory myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms harboring an FGFR1 rearrangement. ZMYM2 and BCR were frequent partners in FIGHT-203.

decisions.label: PCM1::JAK2
decisions.replacement_text: In a series including eight PCM1::JAK2 and one BCR::JAK2 case, ruxolitinib produced hematologic or cytogenetic responses in some patients, but most discontinued for resistance, progression or planned transplantation.

evidence.location: Results 3.2: Response to ruxolitinib; Table 1 and treatment-course Figure 1; PDF pages 3-6
evidence.scope: Actual mixed-JAK2-fusion clinical series; outcomes pooled rather than assigned independently to PCM1.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: Ruxolitinib responses have been described in small series of PCM1::JAK2- and BCR::JAK2-positive myeloid neoplasms; this is off-label fusion-directed evidence.

decisions.label: ZBTB16::RARA
decisions.replacement_text: ZBTB16::RARA was RT-PCR-confirmed in 18 patients in a 24-patient series of rare RARA-rearranged AML with APL-like morphology.

evidence.location: Body cohort molecular-results paragraph preceding Figure 1; Table 1 and Supplementary Table 1
evidence.scope: Exact observed fusion/disease phenotype; structural/corepressor extrapolations excluded.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion retains RARA DNA- and ligand-binding regions within an abnormal transcriptional regulator that blocks myeloid differentiation. It produces an APL-like leukemia with a molecular mechanism distinct from PML::RARA.

decisions.label: NPM1::RARA
decisions.replacement_text: NPM1::RARA was confirmed by RT-qPCR in an infant with AML, a t(5;17) rearrangement and a mandibular myeloid sarcoma in a Hungarian clinical cohort.

evidence.location: Original-cohort Results sections 3.3.1 and 3.5; Figure 5; Table 4
evidence.scope: Root inspected original own-patient case data, not the review portion of this article; exact fusion and phenotype.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion retains RARA DNA- and ligand-binding regions within an abnormal transcriptional regulator that blocks myeloid differentiation. It produces an APL-like leukemia with a molecular mechanism distinct from PML::RARA.

decisions.label: STAT5B::RARA
decisions.replacement_text: STAT5B::RARA was RT-PCR-confirmed in 3 patients in a 24-patient series of rare RARA-rearranged AML with APL-like morphology.

evidence.location: Body cohort molecular-results paragraph preceding Figure 1; Table 1 and Supplementary Table 1
evidence.scope: Exact observed fusion/disease phenotype; structural/corepressor extrapolations excluded.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: The fusion retains RARA DNA- and ligand-binding regions within an abnormal transcriptional regulator that blocks myeloid differentiation. It produces an APL-like leukemia with a molecular mechanism distinct from PML::RARA.

decisions.label: ZBTB16::RARA
decisions.replacement_text: In the rare-RARA series, no evident ATRA/ATO-induced differentiation was observed in ZBTB16::RARA-positive cases despite frequent retinoid exposure; treatment responses to combination regimens do not establish retinoid sensitivity.

evidence.location: Treatment Results; paragraph beginning Most importantly; Figure 1 and Supplementary Table 1
evidence.scope: Actual on-treatment differentiation observation rather than universal treatment-failure claim.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: ZBTB16::RARA and STAT5B::RARA leukemias have shown resistance to ATRA and arsenic-based differentiation treatment; the high sensitivity of conventional PML::RARA APL must not be transferred to these fusions.

decisions.label: NPM1::RARA
decisions.replacement_text: The reported infant with NPM1::RARA-positive AML achieved remission with an AML chemotherapy regimen plus ATRA and remained in first remission at the reported 36-month follow-up. Subsequent treatment included arsenic; this combination outcome does not establish isolated ATRA sensitivity.

evidence.location: Original-cohort Results section 3.6; Table 4 molecular follow-up
evidence.scope: Actual combination regimen and outcome in one fusion-positive patient; no monotherapy extrapolation.

decisions.rationale: Primary body observation supports this claim-scoped replacement; no broader claim is certified.
decisions.original_text: ATRA responsiveness has been reported with NPM1::RARA, but evidence comes from rare variant-APL cases and does not establish the standard PML::RARA ATRA/arsenic regimen for this fusion.

decisions.label: IGH / BCL2
decisions.replacement_text: IGH/BCL2 translocations occur in follicular lymphoma. Whole-genome sequencing directly identified the rearrangement in patient tumors.
decisions.current_text: IGH/BCL2 translocations occur in follicular lymphoma. Whole-genome sequencing directly identified the rearrangement in patient tumors.

evidence.location: Results, BCL2 and BCL6 translocations in FLs; Figure4D and FiguresS1D-G
evidence.scope: Direct BCL2-IGH structural variant observations in follicular lymphoma; no global outcome or functional enhancer assay inferred.

decisions.rationale: Replaced review-only classification support with an inspected primary structural-variant Results passage; removed untested expression mechanism and cross-tumor extensions.
decisions.original_text: The t(14;18) rearrangement places BCL2 under immunoglobulin regulatory control, increasing antiapoptotic BCL2 expression. It is characteristic of conventional follicular lymphoma and occurs in other germinal-center-derived B-cell lymphomas.

decisions.label: IGH / CCND1
decisions.replacement_text: IGH/CCND1 rearrangements are documented in mantle cell lymphoma and plasma cell myeloma. A sequenced mantle cell lymphoma case had a cryptic insertion of intact CCND1 into IGH; optical genome mapping also identified IGH/CCND1 events in myeloma.
decisions.current_text: IGH/CCND1 rearrangements are documented in mantle cell lymphoma and plasma cell myeloma. A sequenced mantle cell lymphoma case had a cryptic insertion of intact CCND1 into IGH; optical genome mapping also identified IGH/CCND1 events in myeloma.

evidence.location: Figure1A-I and Figure2C-D, patient pathology and mate-pair-sequencing junction/insertion plots
evidence.scope: CCND1-positive MCL with an intact CCND1 insertion into IGH; routine FISH-negative cryptic event. Primary figure captions inspected at PMID31015206.

evidence.location: Primary results paragraphs describing IGH rearrangements; Figure1c,e; publisher lines301,312
evidence.scope: IGH rearrangements with CCND1(28),FGFR3/NSD2(12),MAF(4),MAFB(2); exact structural/disease observations, not functional expression tests.

decisions.rationale: Primary patient figures and cohort Results support both disease associations; avoided implying every IGH/CCND1 event has the same breakpoint architecture.
decisions.original_text: The t(11;14) rearrangement increases cyclin D1 expression through IGH regulatory control and promotes cell-cycle progression. It is characteristic of mantle cell lymphoma and also defines a major plasma cell myeloma subgroup.

decisions.label: IGH / CCND2
decisions.replacement_text: IGH/CCND2 rearrangements were detected by FISH in three of 40 cyclin-D1-negative, SOX11-positive mantle cell lymphomas. These are distinct from the more frequent CCND2 rearrangements involving immunoglobulin light-chain loci.
decisions.current_text: IGH/CCND2 rearrangements were detected by FISH in three of 40 cyclin-D1-negative, SOX11-positive mantle cell lymphomas. These are distinct from the more frequent CCND2 rearrangements involving immunoglobulin light-chain loci.

evidence.location: Results, FISH screening for CCND2 and CCND3 translocations, mRNA expression, and gene mutations; Figure2A-C; Table2
evidence.scope: Three IGH-CCND2 cases among40 cyclin-D1-negative/SOX11-positive MCLs; light-chain partners separately identified.

decisions.rationale: Used exact IGH-positive primary cases rather than transferring the light-chain enhancer-hijacking mechanism to IGH.
decisions.original_text: Immunoglobulin enhancer juxtaposition increases CCND2 expression and can substitute for cyclin D1 activation in a subset of cyclin D1-negative mantle cell lymphomas. These events require an appropriate mantle-cell morphologic and phenotypic classification.

decisions.label: IGH / CCND3
decisions.replacement_text: An IGH/CCND3 t(6;14) rearrangement was identified by cytogenetics and FISH in a cyclin-D1-negative mantle cell lymphoma. This patient observation is distinct from cryptic CCND3 rearrangements involving light-chain enhancers.
decisions.current_text: An IGH/CCND3 t(6;14) rearrangement was identified by cytogenetics and FISH in a cyclin-D1-negative mantle cell lymphoma. This patient observation is distinct from cryptic CCND3 rearrangements involving light-chain enhancers.

evidence.location: Table2, case6, cytogenetic and FISH results; Results CCND3-associated rearrangement
evidence.scope: Exact t(6;14)/IGH-CCND3 patient event in cyclin-D1-negative MCL; not evidence transferred from light-chain enhancer insertions.

decisions.rationale: Exact primary Table2 case6 supports the ordered partner pair. Removed generic mechanism inferred from a later light-chain cohort.
decisions.original_text: Immunoglobulin enhancer juxtaposition increases CCND3 expression and can substitute for cyclin D1 activation in a subset of cyclin D1-negative mantle cell lymphomas. These events require an appropriate mantle-cell morphologic and phenotypic classification.

decisions.label: IGH / MALT1
decisions.replacement_text: IGH/MALT1 t(14;18) rearrangements occur in MALT lymphoma. Primary dual-fusion FISH and expression studies documented the rearrangement and increased MALT1 mRNA and protein in affected tumors.
decisions.current_text: IGH/MALT1 t(14;18) rearrangements occur in MALT lymphoma. Primary dual-fusion FISH and expression studies documented the rearrangement and increased MALT1 mRNA and protein in affected tumors.

evidence.location: Results, Correlation of MALT1 and BCL10 protein expression with their mRNA expression; Figure3, Figure4, Figure5; page298
evidence.scope: IGH-MALT1 dual-fusion FISH and higher MALT1 mRNA/protein in rearranged MALT lymphomas. Primary body passage and captions inspected.

decisions.rationale: Primary Figure3 and expression Results/Figure5 substantiate the pair and deregulated expression; no treatment or prognosis extrapolation.
decisions.original_text: The t(14;18) involving MALT1 increases MALT1 expression through IGH regulatory control and activates NF-kappaB-associated survival signaling. It is distinct from the t(14;18) involving BCL2.

decisions.label: IGH / BCL10
decisions.replacement_text: In t(1;14)-positive MALT lymphomas, the BCL10 locus is relocated to the derivative chromosome 14. Primary Northern-blot analysis demonstrated BCL10 overexpression in three such tumors.
decisions.current_text: In t(1;14)-positive MALT lymphomas, the BCL10 locus is relocated to the derivative chromosome 14. Primary Northern-blot analysis demonstrated BCL10 overexpression in three such tumors.

evidence.location: Main Results paragraphs adjacent to Figure2b, BCL10 genomic structure; Figure2b Northern-blot experiments
evidence.scope: BCL10 gene moved to der14 and overexpressed in three t(1;14)-positive MALT lymphomas; direct genomic/expression observations.

decisions.rationale: Retained directly measured genomic relocation and expression rather than a uniform downstream NF-kappaB or clinical claim.
decisions.original_text: The t(1;14) increases BCL10 expression and promotes signaling through the BCL10-MALT1/NF-kappaB pathway. It is a recurrent regulatory rearrangement in MALT lymphoma.

decisions.label: IGH / DUX4
decisions.replacement_text: In a primary B-cell precursor ALL cohort, partial DUX4 copies were inserted into IGH and associated with DUX4 overexpression. DNA sequencing confirmed the rearrangements; most characterized products retained both DUX4 homeodomains while truncating its carboxy terminus.

evidence.location: Results, genomic confirmation of DUX4 rearrangements; Figure3, Supplementary Figures2-3, Supplementary Data6/8
evidence.scope: Partial DUX4 copies inserted into IGH; DNA and RNA confirmation, DUX4 overexpression and preserved homeodomains; no obligatory chimeric protein.

decisions.original_text: Insertion or rearrangement of the repetitive DUX4 locus into IGH regulatory architecture causes abnormal DUX4 expression and a distinctive B-ALL transcriptional program, frequently with secondary ERG alterations.

evidence.location: Results and discussion, NGS-capture analysis of1533 T-ALL/T-LBL patients; Figure1A and TableS1

decisions.label: EWSR1::WT1

evidence.location: Results: EWS-WT1 depletion leads to strong changes in chromatin activity and 3D connectivity; Figures 3, 5 and 6
evidence.scope: Indexed full Results and figure legends: depletion reduces active chromatin and direct target expression; EWS prion-like domain mutants lose binding/activation; coexpression of KTS isoforms generates DSRCT-like xenografts.

decisions.rationale: Primary Results and Figures 3/5/6 establish fusion-dependent transcription and tumor formation in specified model; removed generalized intra-abdominal dissemination statement. No clinical CDK4/6 benefit inferred from preclinical experiments.
decisions.replacement_text: EWSR1::WT1 is an oncogenic transcriptional regulator of desmoplastic small round cell tumor. Fusion-depletion experiments reduce active chromatin, three-dimensional enhancer contacts and direct target-gene expression; coexpression of its +KTS and −KTS splice isoforms generated DSRCT-like xenografts in a mesothelial-cell model.
decisions.original_text: The fusion joins the EWSR1 activation region to WT1 zinc-finger DNA-binding sequences, converting WT1-associated transcription into an oncogenic program. It is characteristic of desmoplastic small round cell tumor, typically presenting with disseminated intra-abdominal disease.

decisions.label: EWSR1::DDIT3

evidence.location: Results; Figure 2
evidence.scope: Fusion-targeted RNA sequencing detected EWSR1-DDIT3 in a myxoid liposarcoma with negative DDIT3 break-apart FISH and diffuse DDIT3 expression. No direct EWSR1-DDIT3 differentiation-block experiment.

decisions.rationale: Results and Figure 2 provide direct molecularly confirmed myxoid liposarcoma observation; FUS-DDIT3 adipogenic mechanism is not extrapolated.
decisions.replacement_text: EWSR1::DDIT3 is a myxoid liposarcoma fusion confirmed by RNA sequencing. A directly documented tumor had diffuse DDIT3 expression despite a negative DDIT3 break-apart FISH result.
decisions.original_text: The fusion joins a FET-family activation region to DDIT3, creating an abnormal transcription factor that disrupts adipocytic differentiation. EWSR1::DDIT3 supports the diagnosis of myxoid liposarcoma; FUS is the usual partner and EWSR1 is less common.

decisions.original_text: The fusion combines a FET-family activation region with a CREB-family DNA-binding region, producing abnormal transcriptional activation. FUS::ATF1 is a recognized fusion in angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma.

decisions.label: CIC::DUX4

evidence.location: Results 3.1–3.2; Figures 1–2; Table S5
evidence.scope: ChIP-seq and fusion depletion in patient-derived CDS cell lines plus primary tumor chromatin profiles: CIC-DUX4-associated active chromatin; direct targets including ETV1/4/5 decrease after depletion.

decisions.rationale: Direct Results 3.1–3.2 and Figures 1–2 demonstrate target activation and fusion dependence. Removed unverified frequency superlative.

In patient-derived cell models, fusion depletion reduced active chromatin and direct target-gene expression, including ETV1, ETV4 and ETV5; primary tumors shared the associated active chromatin pattern.
decisions.original_text: The fusion converts CIC-associated transcriptional repression into an oncogenic ETS-target activation program. It is the most frequent fusion in CIC-rearranged sarcoma, a molecularly distinct disease from Ewing sarcoma.

decisions.original_text: CIC-rearranged sarcoma showed substantially worse survival than BCOR::CCNB3 sarcoma in the retrospective GRACefUl cohort.

decisions.label: BCOR::CCNB3

evidence.location: Results: BCOR-CCNB3 fusions identified by FISH and RNA sequencing; Figures 3–4; Clinical follow-up and Figure 7
evidence.scope: Indexed primary Results: BCOR exon 15-CCNB3 exon 5 junction, inversion FISH, distinct expression cluster; survival comparison of 22 followed BCS versus 57 historical CIC-rearranged controls and ES controls.

decisions.rationale: Direct fusion sequencing, FISH and clustering support the structural alteration and molecular distinction; no untested chromatin-regulatory causation asserted.
decisions.replacement_text: BCOR::CCNB3 is associated with a round-to-spindle-cell sarcoma group. Primary molecular analyses demonstrated the BCOR exon 15–CCNB3 exon 5 junction and inversion-associated FISH pattern, with an expression profile distinct from Ewing and CIC-rearranged sarcomas.
decisions.original_text: An X-chromosome inversion joins BCOR to CCNB3 and creates an abnormal transcriptional/chromatin-regulatory product. It defines a distinct round-cell sarcoma that often affects adolescent males.

decisions.label: BCOR::CCNB3

evidence.location: Results: BCOR-CCNB3 fusions identified by FISH and RNA sequencing; Figures 3–4; Clinical follow-up and Figure 7
evidence.scope: Indexed primary Results: BCOR exon 15-CCNB3 exon 5 junction, inversion FISH, distinct expression cluster; survival comparison of 22 followed BCS versus 57 historical CIC-rearranged controls and ES controls.

decisions.replacement_text: In a molecularly confirmed BCOR::CCNB3 series, the 22 patients with follow-up had a five-year overall survival estimate of 72%, better than the historical CIC-rearranged sarcoma control cohort. Seven of nine evaluable tumors treated with Ewing-type chemotherapy showed 60–100% treatment-related necrosis or fibrosis.
decisions.original_text: BCOR::CCNB3 sarcoma had better survival than CIC-rearranged sarcoma in the retrospective GRACefUl cohort; many patients received Ewing-type chemotherapy.
